futures.title: More detectors and rule tweaks
futures.description: The scenario gap list and real-code trials keep producing detector work (arithmetic magic numbers, new noise filters). Every new rule touches the detector, the catalog, the location roles it reports and the scenarios.

futures.title: Scoring weights tuned from calibration
futures.description: Calibration on bitwarden/server suggested re-weighting Value and Position; more trials will move strengths, distance weights and the score formula.

futures.title: Published to NuGet with real versioning
futures.description: The README says the tool isn't on NuGet yet. Publishing brings version numbers that must agree everywhere they are written, and release notes. Touches no findings today: the version is written in the .csproj files and in Reports.Version, and the tool doesn't read project files, so it can't link them.

futures.title: Report formats and CI integration grow
futures.description: Teams adopting it will want GitHub annotations, HTML or trend charts; the existing formats share number formats and limits.

futures.title: Finding ids stay stable across versions
futures.description: 0.2.0 changed finding ids and asked users to re-baseline. Once people depend on it, ids will need to survive detector changes (migration of baselines and acceptances). Touches no findings today: Store.cs and the fingerprint code are clean.

futures.title: Real parsers for other languages
futures.description: Generic mode is text-based. TypeScript or Python projects would need syntax-aware analysis to reach C# quality.

futures.title: Roslyn analyzer catches up with the CLI
futures.description: The analyzer package reports C# findings per project and has no tests. Users in the IDE will expect cross-project and futures-aware results.

stable.reason: Git plumbing (staged files, diffs, churn) follows git's own output formats, which don't change.
